transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I keep losing interest in the projects and activities I usually care about, even when everything in my life is going fine. My girlfriend really started noticing these patterns and suggested I seek some help, which is what prompted me to get this evaluation.

You mentioned your girlfriend noticed patterns. Have you ever experienced periods where you felt the exact opposite—such as having unusually high energy, feeling on top of the world, or needing very little sleep?

Yeah, I definitely get these stretches where I feel totally amped up and wake up buzzing with energy, ready to tackle a million projects without feeling tired. My mind starts racing so fast at night that I can't sleep, and I get this feeling that I have a grand vision and could easily run my own design firm. I can also get pretty easily irritated during those times if my girlfriend or anyone questions my ideas.
How long do these high-energy periods typically last, and how many years have you been experiencing this pattern of shifting between highs and lows?
Those high-energy stretches usually only last for a few days at a time. I'd say I've been experiencing this whole cycle of shifting between the highs and lows off and on for about a year now.
When you experience those low periods where you lose interest, how long do they typically last at a time, and how severely do they impact your daily life or work?

This current low spell has been hanging around in some form for most of the past year, lasting much longer than the quick high bursts. It's made me really unreliable—I've missed work deadlines, bailed on community projects, and my girlfriend says she doesn't know which version of me she's coming home to.
You mentioned these shifts have been happening for about a year. Have you ever experienced similar, perhaps milder, ups and downs further back in your past, going back two years or more?

Looking back, I think similar patterns probably strained some of my past relationships and commitments further back. But as far as these really distinct, noticeable cycles go, I can only clearly recall them happening off and on for about the last year.
During those high-energy times, have they ever lasted for four or more days in a row, or are they always shorter than that?
Yes, they usually last right around four or five days in a row. After that stretch, the high energy starts to fade and I'll shift back down.
During those high-energy times, have you ever had an episode that lasted a full week or longer, or have you ever needed to be hospitalized because the energy became unsafe or out of control?

No, those high-energy periods have never lasted a full week, usually just a few days at a time. I've also never been hospitalized or felt so out of control that it became unsafe. It gets intense, but it has never reached that point.
During these low periods, do you experience feelings of worthlessness, extreme guilt, or any thoughts of self-harm or suicide?

When I'm in those low spells, I feel like a terrible boyfriend and team lead, constantly replaying my mistakes and thinking my girlfriend would be better off without me. On the worst nights, I'll lie in bed thinking it wouldn't really matter if I didn't wake up tomorrow, though I don't have any actual plan to harm myself.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a pattern of mood shifts characterized by distinct hypomanic episodes and major depressive episodes. The hypomanic episodes last 4-5 days (meeting the minimum 4-day threshold) and feature increased energy, grandiosity, racing thoughts, decreased need for sleep, and irritability, without causing severe impairment or requiring hospitalization. The depressive episodes are characterized by loss of interest, feelings of worthlessness/guilt, and passive suicidal ideation, resulting in significant occupational and interpersonal impairment. This clinical presentation is diagnostic of Bipolar II Disorder (ICD-10: F31.8).
